text:
Polished diagram in the review. Twelve boxes, clean arrows.

Then: "What happens when Redis goes down?"

Cache was on the slide. Nothing said fail-open, fail-closed, or whether we'd stampede the database.

Requirements and napkin math were done — the drawing still didn't show read vs write paths, solid vs async, or the consistency choices we'd already written down.

I wrote how I layer diagrams now: context → high-level → one data flow → failure boundaries; solid vs dashed arrows; short labels on the hot path.
